$comment: v2 MCP configuration — a template. Nothing here is live; every REPLACE_ME is yours to fill.
The difference from v1 is not which servers exist. It is who the call is made as.
v1 (.github/mcp.json): the session is already signed in, so a server inherits that session's identity implicitly.
v2 (this file): a container has no session. Each server must be told, per call, whose authority it is acting under,
and must refuse the call when it cannot establish one. There is deliberately no shared credential in this file.

identity.$comment: Read by the runner before any server is contacted. These are the rules, not a connection.
identity.source: the identity supplied with the request that triggered this run
identity.$failClosedMeaning: If a caller identity cannot be established and forwarded, the run stops. It does not fall back to the container's own identity, and it does not fall back to a service account.

audit.$comment: One line per tool call, not one line per run. 'Which agent touched which source on whose behalf' should be answerable without reading a transcript.

defaults.$comment: Applied to every server below unless that server overrides it.
defaults.$networkMeaning: Reachable only from the fleet's own network. A source that must be reached over the public internet is a deliberate exception and says so.

issues.$comment: Read the work. A runner that can close an issue can close the wrong one, so this one cannot write.

repo.$comment: Read code and open branches. Merging is not here on purpose — that is a human gate, in v1 and v2 alike.
repo.$denyMeaning: Named here as well as in tools/hooks/guard.py. The hook is the enforcement; this list is so a reader of the config knows the rule exists without reading Python.

ci.$comment: Read build and test results. Triggering a run is allowed; changing the pipeline is not.

docs.$comment: Reference material. The one server that may legitimately be public, so it says so rather than inheriting 'private' silently.

messaging.$comment: The exception that proves the rule. Present so a runner can READ context from a thread. Sending is absent and denied, because customer-facing communication is drafts only and a human sends. If you add a send tool here, you have broken the fleet's central promise.

perAgent.$comment: Each agent sees only the servers its role needs. This mirrors the tools allowlist already declared in .github/agents/<name>.agent.md — the agent file is the source of truth, and this is how that declaration becomes a network boundary rather than a suggestion.
